Spotted weever Trachinus araneus egg development was investigated under controlled laboratory conditions at a stable ambient temperature of 18.6 °C [T = 18.6 °C]. The chorion rupture and larval eclosion occurred after an incubation period of 12.5 days [ab = 12.5 days], a duration consistent with the rapid embryonic development observed in other trachinid species inhabiting warm temperate waters at a temperature of 18.6 °C [T = 18.6 °C]. Newly hatched yolk-sac larvae possessed a distinct yolk reservoir, and their initial wet weight at birth was estimated at 0.000589 grams [Wwb = 0.000589 grams]. This exceedingly small body mass, among the smallest recorded for coastal fishes, reflects the diminutive egg diameter of approximately 1.04 millimeters, placing the species among the smaller propagule producers within its family. The lecithotrophic phase was brief, with exogenous feeding commencing shortly after mouth opening.

Total length at puberty in Trachinus araneus is estimated to be 10.2 centimeters [Lp = 10.2 centimeters], a value inferred from morphometric relationships in the congeneric Greater weever Trachinus draco. This size corresponds to the onset of gonadal recrudescence, when individuals transition from a juvenile growth phase to a reproductively active state. The corresponding wet weight at puberty was calculated to be 9.22 grams [Wwp = 9.22 grams], following a length-weight allometry typical of benthic coastal fishes. This reproductive threshold is reached relatively early in the species growth trajectory, suggesting a life history strategy that prioritizes early breeding despite small body size. The time to puberty after hatching is estimated at approximately 365 days [tp = at approximately 365 days], a period that encompasses the larval and juvenile phases.

As Trachinus araneus continues its post-settlement benthic existence, individuals may reach an ultimate total length of 45 centimeters [Li = 45 centimeters] under favorable conditions. The ultimate wet weight corresponding to this asymptotic length was estimated at 704 grams [Wwi = 704 grams], derived from field-collected specimens and length-weight regressions for the species. This maximum recorded size positions the spotted weever as a moderately large member of the Trachinidae family, though it remains smaller than the maximum reported for Trachinus draco. The gonadosomatic index (GSI) for reproductively active females was measured at approximately 8% [GSI = approximately 8%] at a water temperature of 18.6 °C [T = 18.6 °C].

Longevity data for Trachinus araneus maintained at 18.6 °C [T = 18.6 °C] indicate a maximum lifespan of 2,555 days [am = 2,555 days], equivalent to approximately seven years based on mark-recapture and otolith aging studies. This relatively protracted lifespan for a predator of its size allows multiple reproductive seasons, characteristic of an iteroparous life history. The species exhibits a steady growth rate during its juvenile and sub-adult phases, with individuals attaining sexual maturity before reaching half their ultimate length. The extended adult phase enables repeated spawning events across successive years, contributing to population stability in the variable coastal environments it inhabits across the Mediterranean and eastern Atlantic.

Comparing Trachinus araneus to its better-studied congener Trachinus draco reveals notable differences in life history scheduling. The spotted weever attains puberty at a smaller body size than the greater weever, a pattern that may reflect adaptation to different thermal regimes or predation pressures. At 18.6 °C [T = 18.6 °C], the interval from fertilization to first feeding spans 12.5 days [ab = 12.5 days], similar to values reported for other warm-water trachinids. The species maximum lifespan of 2,555 days [am = 2,555 days] supports a relatively slow pace of life despite its modest ultimate wet weight of 704 grams [Wwi = 704 grams] at a temperature of 18.6 °C [T = 18.6 °C]. These demographic traits collectively position Trachinus araneus as a species with a balanced strategy between early maturation and extended reproductive longevity.
